climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Gewürztraminer, Riesling, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc fully without cooking off their freshness.

soil.rock: Sandstone is sand bound into rock. It weathers to light, sandy soil that drains freely. Marl is a limy clay. It holds water and makes vines ripen later, which keeps acidity in the grapes. Clay holds water well but drains poorly. It stays cool, which slows ripening and keeps acidity up.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 2°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.
